methods.label: Use the definition of the y-intercept
methods.explanation: A point on the \(y\)-axis has \(x=0\). Substituting into the line equation gives \(y/3=1\), so \(y=3\). Thus the \(y\)-intercept is \(3\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the coordinate definition of an axis intercept and a simple equation, without requiring intercept-form recognition.
